guide.summary: A slow, long-lived sugar eater that folds up and rests when food runs out.
guide.biology: Some bacteria can switch into a quiet resting form that uses very little energy and waits for better times.
guide.rules: Eats sugar slowly using oxygen and can live up to 1800 seconds. Moves 0.25 cells per second and senses food up to 2 cells away. Stays active in cooler and drier places than most bacteria (warmth from 0.25, moisture from 0.2). After 20 seconds without food, or 10 seconds too dry, with at least 15 energy, it spends 5 seconds and 10 energy folding up. Resting, it does not move or feed, uses 0.01 energy per second and takes one tenth of the usual harm from poor conditions and inhibitors (running out of energy still harms it at the full rate), but can still be eaten. It wakes after 10 seconds of good conditions with food and at least 5 energy, spending 5 seconds and 5 energy, and cannot rest again for 30 seconds.
guide.example: Let the sugar run out in a dish with Sprinters and Sleepers, then add sugar again and see who is still there to eat it.
